device.name: LIFX Z
device.notes:
LIFX Z LED strips support the LIFX binary LAN protocol over UDP port 56700 with no authentication. The observed strips advertise HomeKit HAP over mDNS with md=LIFX Z; consumers can resolve IP address from mDNS and then send a UDP GetService message to port 56700 for full LIFX metadata. LIFX Z is a multizone light strip; common units expose eight zones using HSBK color. The current schema does not have a native UDP endpoint type, so protocol details are captured in protocol_handler and lifx_lan_protocol.
MATTER CAVEAT: LIFX's Matter firmware rollout (Sept 2025) is eligible on LCM3-edition hardware (firmware v3.x) only — the original LIFX Z (firmware v2.x) is excluded — and updating to Matter DECOMMISSIONS the HomeKit/HAP integration. Units that take the Matter update stop advertising _hap._tcp.local., which kills the mDNS discovery signal this spec relies on; discover those units by UDP broadcast GetService instead.

credentials.notes: Post-setup LAN control is unauthenticated UDP on port 56700, so no client credential is issued and anything on the LAN can drive the strip.

factory_reset.effect: Clears WiFi credentials and returns the device to its unprovisioned, AP-hosting state.

procedures.indicator: The light cycles colours to confirm the reset.
procedures.name: Five power cycles

steps.action: Switch the fixture off and on five times, leaving it on for about two seconds each time.
Wait for the colour-cycle confirmation, then look for the setup AP.

methods.description: Unprovisioned devices advertise their own access point named after the product and serial. The vendor app joins it and hands over the home network credentials. Field layout and transport for that exchange are unverified here — capture required before a replacement client can be written.

steps.action: Power the strip and wait for it to advertise its setup AP.
Capture the vendor app's provisioning exchange over that AP.
steps.notes: Open gap: needed to document the credential transfer.

setup.notes: LIFX strips must be joined to WiFi before the LAN protocol is usable. The onboarding exchange itself has not been captured in this project — the device hosts a temporary AP that the vendor app talks to, and the older published LAN protocol had SetAccessPoint/GetAccessPoint messages that are now marked deprecated. Once provisioned, control is unauthenticated UDP and needs no further setup.

rejoin.notes: No documented in-place credential update; treat a router change as a reset-and-reprovision.

http_endpoints.description: Some observed LIFX Z devices have TCP port 80 open, but LAN control is the binary UDP protocol on port 56700.
http_endpoints.name: Optional Embedded HTTP Root

discovery_flow: Browse _hap._tcp.local. and keep records where TXT md is LIFX Z.
Use txt:id as the stable MAC/accessory identifier.
Send LIFX LAN GetService message type 2 to UDP port 56700.
lifx_lan_protocol.message_type_notes: set_power 117 is light-level power (LightSetPower); the device-level SetPower message is 21. set_color 102 sets ALL zones at once — per-zone control needs the multizone family below. Full machine-readable message definitions (pkt_type, sizes, fields) are published officially in the LIFX/public-protocol repo (protocol.yml) — the codegen source for a lifx_lan_udp handler.
